analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and edits the environment-variables paragraph (base 314-315, head 314-316). The edit states that DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS, the delta-checkpoint rollback switch, is on the LaunchAgent passthroughEnvKeys allowlist, alongside DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY. Test-root and persistent-key benchmark controls remain explicitly off the list.

This is documentation-only, with no source or control change visible. The documented behavior would let an operator-set env var reach the launchd daemon and disable delta checkpoints, so complete files are written whole. That is a local operator-controlled availability and wear toggle. It does not alter DBK3 crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL, scope binding or the epoch, so the T-041 mitigations are unchanged. Writing whole files still debits the daily write budget, which the same doc says is enforced.

The doc claim that the variable is allowlisted cannot be verified from LaunchAgent.swift, which was not supplied. If the code does not match, that is a documentation accuracy issue, not a security regression. A later pass should confirm that passthroughEnvKeys contains this key and that no key-material or test-root variable was added to it. Within the supplied evidence, I found no regressions, new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions.
